cd442153b53ec114.heading: Community Investment Tax Relief (Self Assessment helpsheet HS237)

amounts.name: CITR annual relief rate
amounts.period: per tax year, for each of 5 tax years
amounts.value: up to 5% of the invested amount

amounts.name: CITR total maximum relief
amounts.value: up to 25% of the invested amount

amounts.name: Example 3 invested amount entered on return

caveats: CITR is a relief against Income Tax only; it cannot be used to reduce Capital Gains Tax
If Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies, claims and adjustments are made through compatible software instead of the Self Assessment boxes described
Relief may be reduced if part of a loan/deposit is repaid/withdrawn within 5 years, or if the investor receives value, financial advantage or benefit from the CDFI
Investor must be beneficial owner, unprotected from investment risk, and the investment must not be part of a tax avoidance scheme for relief to remain valid
If payments on account are reduced in anticipation of CITR but the relief due is less than expected, HMRC will charge interest on the shortfall
cross_references: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax guidance
Community Investment Tax Relief manual (HMRC CITR manual)

deadlines.name: Earliest point for formal CITR claim
deadlines.rule: Cannot make a formal claim until the Tax Relief Certificate is received and the tax year to which the claim relates has ended

definitions.meaning: Accredited institution in which individuals or companies invest to qualify for CITR; list prepared by BEIS
Certificate issued by the CDFI for each qualifying investment, needed before a formal claim can be made
For shares/securities, the amount subscribed; for loans/deposits, generally the original advance or deposit, subject to reduction if part is repaid/withdrawn within 5 years

obligations.must: Enter the 'invested amount(s)' on which relief is claimed in box 3 in the 'Other tax reliefs' section on page Ai 2 of the Additional Information (SA101) pages
obligations.trigger: Claiming CITR relief for the tax year

obligations.must: Give details about each investment in box 19, 'Any other information', on page TR7 of the tax return
Keep the Tax Relief Certificate safe (do not need to send with return, but may be requested during an enquiry)
obligations.trigger: Receipt of Tax Relief Certificate from CDFI

obligations.must: Write to HMRC to ask for a change to current year's PAYE code to include expected CITR
obligations.trigger: Investor wants relief reflected before formal claim
obligations.who: Individual investor wanting in-year benefit via PAYE

obligations.must: Write to HMRC to ask to reduce Self Assessment payments on account to reflect expected CITR
obligations.trigger: Investor wants relief reflected before formal claim
obligations.who: Individual investor wanting in-year benefit via payments on account

note.summary: HS237 explains how individual investors claim Community Investment Tax Relief (CITR) for investments in accredited Community Development Finance Institutions (CDFIs), giving up to 5% relief per year for 5 tax years (25% total) against Income Tax only. It sets out how to enter the invested amount in box 3 of the Additional Information (SA101) pages and provide details in box 19 of TR7, plus how PAYE codes or payments on account can be adjusted in-year pending formal claim after the tax year ends.
